slides.title: Vehicle Integrated Functionalities Validation
slides.body:
Vehicle Integrated Functionalities Validation Introduction
Why
Introduction:
The validation takes part in several development engineering process, its rule is to define the correctness of a creation
compared to its original concept design.
Why do we validate?
In this case we consider the SW developing. The validation has the purpose to establish if the implemented SW logics in the
development process reflects the specification requirements and if the behaviour of the control system meets the expected
response.
Why in vehicle?
The vehicle integrated functionalities validation (VIF) has the purpose of testing the sw functionalities in a situation where the
control is applied on complex dynamics and there is the interaction between non-simulated ECUs , and in general a real
response by the controlled system is required. This test environment represent the highest qualitative analysis process of an
automotive integrated system : the test are performed in a real controlled system where the answer to a specific stimulus
contains all the dynamics/disturbance that a simulated environment can not provide due to high complexity in terms of
elaboration.

slides.title: Vehicle Integrated Functionalities Validation
slides.body:
Vehicle Integrated Functionalities Validation Introduction
Real vs
Virtual
What are the vehicle validation’s advantages compared to simulated environment?
As we said, the vehicle testing validation does include real system answer to a specific stimulus. A validator can exclude all the
problems caused by the inaccuracy or the limitation of the simulated environment that could negatively affect test results . At
the same time, real application does represent a constraint: it is not possible to force the system in a specific condition so easly
as a simulated environment where all the involved input are arbitrarily choosen by the user. In this case a specific maneuver
(or a sequence) must be applied in order to let the system reach that status (e.g. the thermal engine increment – warm up).
Some test forces the validator to adopt complex strategies in order reaching that required inputs : sensors are real, thus the
read data is defined by a real physical entity.
On the other hand, vehicle validation can prove the simulated system robustness: real testing environment can confirm the
stressed system’s result performed either in a simulated environment in order to prove the correctness and reliability of the
simulation itself.

slides.title: Vehicle Integrated Functionalities Validation

Vehicle Integrated Functionalities Validation Introduction
When VIF?
When is the Vehicle validation performed?
Integrated functionality is the last part of the sw investigation to be performed. Thus vehicle validation usually is performed in
the last stage of the development.

slides.title: Aim
slides.body:
Following the V model , there is a progression in term of HW test environment: from open\closed loop model to the final product .
Vehicle validation process inside the V model occupies the last step of the sw development . A validator has the duty to check the reliability of the controls and
the correct implementation of the sw functionality.
- The Val is performed following a list of test cases extracted from the requirement functionality description: CheckList , DVP (Design Validation Plan).
- System behaviour is measured and analyzed
- As final result, the validator gives feedback through analysis report of the functionality tested compared to the system requirements to the suppliers or
the involved development sw team (Calibrators , Functionists …) . In this way a feedback process inside the V-model is established , introducing where
needed bugfix suggestions and sw modification (Troubleshooting).

slides.title: Design Validation Plan & Results
slides.body:
As we previously said, the validation provides a comparison between the functional concept and the resulting SW implementation.
This process is usually prepared reporting all the specs inside a document where they are translated into a list of maneuver to be executed in vehicle; the test
description must contain all relevant information for the test execution adapted in the environment where it’s applied and togheter fulfill the requirement
concept.
e.g. requirement reports that the thermostatic engine coolant valve must be closed in very first phase of engine warm up, and that ECM starts to command the
opening after that the engine coolant temperature is close to the target idling temp � test case: Turn on the engine and wait for the regimated coolant
temperature between 80° or 90° (depending on engine thermal characteristic), check that thermostatic valve sensed position is fully close for 10 seconds after
that the engine has started and it is partially/fully opened when the engine temp has been regimated.
Once DVP is ready, the validator analyze the behaviour of the system tested and gives Result.

slides.title: Validation Test example - ECM SpeedLimiter Overspeed management
Speed Limiter Overview
slides.body:
Whole ECM Speed Limiter management
The calculation of the speed setpoint is managed entirely by the
engine control unit (that’s why is defined as «whole», in some cases
the speed limiter control is managed by two nodes): it receives
signal from the steering wheel and (with the coordination of the
ESP) defines the output speed limitation driver request , this value is
then published on CAN and is displayed on the instrument cluster.

slides.title: Speed Limiter Overview
slides.body:
Jeep Wrangler Speed Limiter ECUs interaction
The Speed Limiter is a high impact driver function whose main
purpose is to limit the vehicle speed to a maximum threshold .
Nowadays , this function is a standard equipment on almost every
vehicle on the market and it usually implicates the interaction
between at least 2 or more ECUs to elaborate the driver settings .
On PowerNet architecture we have the interaction between SCCM ,
IPC and ECM , the last one has the main duty to elaborate , once
received , the driver command for the speed limitation and actuate
the setpoint track .

slides.title: Engine Cam-Backup strategy VF description
slides.body:
Some functionality tests keep their own significance only when tested in vehicle.
Crankshaft tone wheel back-up strategy:
Engine position is an essential entity; ECM must be able to recognize it in every operational condition. Several strategies directly descended from engine position &
speed calculation (injection control, VVA, gear management, fuel pressure…etc) and contribute to the whole engine operation.
Whether Crankshaft tone wheel signal is corrupted or not available at all, ECM shall be able to calculate the right position using Camshaft tone wheel input value in
order to define the current engine speed. This recovery action is implemented for safety reasons; it guarantees the engine to be operative even in degraded states.
Such a strategy is a required feature which is usually tested during Engine Position Management validation.

slides.title: Engine Cam-Backup strategy VF description
slides.body:
32.11.2.1 Engine Speed Calculation
Engine speed/RPM shall be calculated internally in the ECU from crank sensor teeth period (tooth to tooth time) as soon as valid crank teeth information is available AND while valid top dead center
information is not yet available.
Top Dead Center Positions shall be considered valid for computing rpm once the crank position bus is locked and the two TDC positions have been traversed.
IF valid TDC information is available, engine speed/RPM shall be calculated internally in the ECU from two TDCs, and no longer from crank sensor teeth period.
Engine speed/RPM shall also be calculated from the cam position sensor(s) IF the cam position sensor(s) are locked AND two TDC positions have been traversed.
IF the crank sensor is not faulted/failed, Engine speed/RPM shall be reported over CAN from the valid crank sensor.
IF the crank sensor is faulted/failed AND the cam sensor is not faulted/failed, the engine speed/RPM shall be reported over CAN from the valid cam sensor signal
Engine speed will be calculated down to the point where the active/valid sensor (crank or cam) becomes unlocked, and at the point the RPM signal is ramped down to "0".
Engine speed will be calculated up to 8160 RPM and sent on the bus in ECM_A1.EngRPM
Engine speed shall be sent on the bus in ECM_A1.EngRPM
Cam BackUp

slides.title: BackUp SW management
slides.body:
ECM is able to detect every tooth transition and recognizes crankshaft edges; tooth counting is buffered and internally processed in order to obtain the segment
period; this information defines the engine speed. If a single or multiple tooth is not available (where expected) the ECM recognizes the issue; consequently, the
injection is no more applied � the engine comes to stop.
After 7 crankshaft revolutions with systematic missing tooth, Crankshaft source is recognized as faulty (calibratible issue debounce). As a consequence, CAM
BackUp strategy is applied (in this scenario a Diagnostic Fault is expected).
In the same way, if Crankshaft signal is not available the ECM will adopt a filtering phase waiting for 7 crankshaft revolutions - calculated by Camshaft signal
(Crankshaft & Camshaft position are strictly related) - before applying Cam-BackUp strategy.
When BackUp strategy is applied, if the actual engine speed (calculated by CamShaft signal) is greater than a fixed threshold (ex. 500 RPM), the ECM will pilot the
injection in order to keep the idle engine speed, otherwise the engine will be shutted down.

slides.title: Conclusions: Environmental significance
slides.body:
When CrankShaft LoS has been performed in idle conditions, two different results stand out from different testing environment.
When HiL-tested, Cam BackUp strategy correctly worked with a 8/10 successful ratio of engine idling recovering. This means that for 8 cases in 10 if the
Crankshaft signal was suddenly missing - in idle conditions- the ECM was able to correctly adopt backup strategy in order to keep the engine “alive”.
On the contrary, when vehicle-tested, the ratio dropped down to approximately 5/10.
This other ratio was due to actual engine physical behaviour, different from the simulated one: some model dynamics (such as frictions losses, mechanical
inertia, etc…) were not reliable and it had a big impact on this kind of analysis.
This example shows how test significance depends on the performing environment and, moreover, not every test can be reproduced in a simulated one.

slides.title: Appendix ▪
slides.body:
▪ Calibration – Nowadays, a large variety of engine vehicle hardware layout are under the domain of a
common compatibile electronic unit. This means that in some case the engine electronic architecture is
likely the same for two or more different vehicle models (this in particular for the models of a specific
manufacturer), thus same engine SW might be applied on: different engines version can be managed
by a same electronic unit with a common code. How can we let a 1.6l 120hp manual transmission and
a 2.0l 180hp automatic transmission be managed by the same software application? The answer is
calibration. The calibration process has the purpose to adapt the applicative software for that specific
system. In terms of control, it allows the SW to work correctly using the polivalent controls logic coded
tooned to that engine application. In the end, the software is able to manage either 1.6 manual and 2.0
automatic transmission, through calibration it is possible to define the control output.

slides.title: Appendix ▪
slides.body:
▪ ETK – Emulator-Tastkopf (emulator test probe). Specific hardware (usually integrated) device, so
called «development ECUs» that allows an user to analyze and modify the control logic supported by
the SW. ETK interface is supported by ETAS tools and devices. Tools such INCA allows an engineer to
monitor real time internal sw (high level entity) values and modify through calibration control logic. An
emulator test probe (ETK) is installed in the control unit for the parallel application. The ETK is
connected to all bus lines of the control unit processor and replaces either the control unit program and
the calibration data or the calibration data only – depending on the control unit. Consequently, the
calibration system can change control parameters online. Furthermore, the ETK provides RAM
(socalled DPR = Dual Port RAM) to transfer measured data from the control unit to the calibration
system. The ETK is the control unit-specific component of the memory emulation.

slides.title: Appendix ▪
slides.body:
▪ CCP/XCP - CAN Calibration Protocol/ eXtended Calibration Protocol. Both protocols are finalized to
the calibration use through conventional interfaces different from ETK, they enable read and write
access to variables and memory contents of microcontroller systems at runtime (even sw flashing).
CCP is a protocol standardized on the CAN bus. XCP uses more interfaces options based on different
communication protocols such as CAN, FlexRay, Ethernet or USB.
